title.title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
title.subtitle: Claim: a real Banach space with Markov type $p > 1$ is superreflexive, which closes a Ribe-program question

plain: If random walks inside a space never spread faster than ordinary diffusion, must the space be nicely round?

beats.text: Schematic: Markov type asks that a reversible random walk spread no faster than diffusively
In any space that is not superreflexive, the claim builds walks that travel linearly in time
So nontrivial Markov type forces superreflexivity; the converse was known

steps: Suppose the space is not superreflexive
Then build reversible walks that travel in a straight line
Straight-line travel breaks Markov type: contradiction

achievement.label: Naor's question (Ribe program, 2012, Question 4)
statement: X \text{ has Markov type } p > 1 \iff X \text{ is superreflexive}
achievement.context: Before: superreflexive implies Markov type (Naor–Peres–Schramm–Sheffield, 2006); converse open

verify.detail: The full equivalence, Markov type against an equivalent uniformly convex norm, about 27k lines
verify.ourCheck: We read the review of the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: A random walk in a space. Markov type says it spreads no faster than diffusion.
Without superreflexivity, random walks travel in straight lines, which breaks Markov type.
Claimed: nontrivial Markov type forces superreflexivity.

sources.quote: Converse asked by Naor, 'An introduction to the Ribe program', Japan. J. Math. 7 (2012), Question 4.
Naor-Peres-Schramm-Sheffield (Duke Math. J. 2006, 'Markov chains in smooth Banach spaces...') proved p-uniformly smooth implies Markov type p, so superreflexive implies nontrivial Markov type.
Markov type, introduced by Ball in 1992, asks whether a stationary reversible random walk mapped into a space spreads no faster than diffusively.
In a non-superreflexive space, James–Enflo finite representability gives a spreading norm in which you can build reversible chains whose displacement grows linearly in time.
